name: Patrice Lumumba
role: First prime minister of the Republic of the Congo (June-September 1960); leader of the Congolese National Movement
summary: Congolese nationalist and pan-Africanist who led the MNC to independence in 1960 and opposed colonial discrimination and exploitation. He favoured a unitary state, rejected Katanga's secession, practised positive neutrality in the cold war and favoured state-led development. In the crisis he appealed to the UN and the Soviet Union and defended Parliament's authority until his arrest and killing.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposed every secession: pledged to fight 'every attempt to dislocate our national territory', denounced Katanga's secession and federalist proposals as imperialist division.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: As prime minister he sent the national army against Katanga and said troops were impatient to enter Katanga to 'liberate' it; asked the UN to help suppress the secession.

decide-locally.rationale: Insisted on a unified, centralised state and told youth to combat 'federalism, federation or confederation' as imperialist devices.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Defended the Congo's colonial-era territorial entity ('preservation of its political and economic entity') against partition.

national-self-determination.rationale: Demanded immediate, complete independence for the Congo and for all colonies; 'Algeria is not French, Angola is not Portuguese'.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned colonial rule as forced labour, seizure of land and exploitation, and demanded its abolition.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rejected delay or transition: 'There can be no compromise between freedom and slavery', whatever positive aspects of the colonial system.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Denounced laws that treated blacks and whites differently, pledged to eradicate all discrimination and to guarantee the Declaration of Human Rights freedoms to all citizens.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Denounced racially segregated housing, cinemas, restaurants and transport and demanded immediate elimination of racial discrimination and colonial-era unjust laws.

racial-franchise.rationale: Called the colonial equal-seats arrangement for the European minority and African majority anti-democratic; sought a democratic state with equality and no discrimination.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Pledged to eradicate all discrimination whatever its origin and condemned whites-only shops, restaurants and cinemas.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Demanded eradication of every vestige of colonialism, notably racial discrimination and unjust colonial laws, and Africanisation of the administration.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sought a Congolese nation of many tribes in which Europeans who stayed would also share; fought tribalism as a poison.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Adopted 'positive neutralism': 'neither a Western nor a communist bloc'; refused to make the Congo an arena of the cold war.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Declared that Africa refuses to keep imperialist armed forces on its soil ('no more Bizertes, Kitonas, Kaminas') and demanded Belgian withdrawal from Kamina and Kitona.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Repeatedly stated that Belgium and imperialist powers were organising Katanga's secession to divide the Congo and recapture its wealth, and that some powers sought its dismemberment.

non-intervention.rationale: Protested Belgian and UN interference in internal affairs and said no foreign power may enter without the legal government's request; yet he himself asked the UN to intervene against Belgium and Katanga.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Appealed to the UN and asked it for military assistance, but then denounced the Secretary-General's 'interference' and threatened to dispense with its services.

dominated-front.rationale: Called on African states to form a united resistance front against imperialist powers while rejecting entry into cold-war blocs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Sought a Pan-African bloc and 'African unity' decided by heads of state, while insisting on national sovereignty; the form of union was not specified.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Built and defended the Congolese National Army: 'We have our own armies to defend our countries'.

state-harmful.rationale: Founded and led a national government and, in scholars' summary, saw state intervention as necessary for equality, justice and social harmony.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Saw the state as an advocate of public welfare, promising social justice and fair remuneration, state-led development.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Favoured state-led economic development and agreed a state development corporation (CIMCO) as prime minister.

national-resource-control.rationale: Said Katanga and Kasai intrigues aimed to recapture economic control, vowed Congolese would not be exploited again and that the lands must benefit their children; pledged to 'preserve our resources'.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said legal independence was only the first step and called for a national economy and economic independence that improves worker and peasant living standards; did not specify a property-system transformation.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Urged building a national economy and economic independence, yet welcomed foreign aid and technical help not aimed at imposing a policy.

property-fundamental.rationale: Pledged respect for capital investment and the property of residents, but condemned colonial land seizures and his government nationalised Belga offices.

democracy-best.rationale: Wanted a 'modern democratic state' and a 'land of democracy and freedom', and defended an elected parliament as sovereign.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Argued a government may be dismissed only when it loses the people's trust and Parliament's confidence, and proposed a referendum to let the people choose their leaders.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Called Parliament 'the only sovereign body in the country' and 'the country's supreme organ', over the head of state.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Proposed in November 1960 a referendum on a presidential regime followed by direct election of the President.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: As prime minister decreed a state of emergency, an ordinance against 'trouble-makers' and gathering approvals, and identity checks.

party-controls-media.rationale: Restricted the press and nationalised Belga offices into a state news agency, though he also decried Kasavubu's curbs on majority newspapers.

revolution-justified.rationale: Called himself a revolutionary and the youth 'standard-bearers of the peaceful revolution'; won independence by negotiation while praising the armed and unarmed struggle.

political-violence-never.rationale: Recalled independence as won through 'tears, fire and blood' and spoke of struggle, but stressed peaceful negotiation and peace.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Aimed to revive Africa's cultural, philosophical, social and moral values.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rejected the colonialists' 'stupid superiority complex' and the claim of African backwardness.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Named tribalism and religious separatism among the obstacles to a harmonious African society.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honoured fighters who died for independence: 'Eternal glory to the fighters for national liberation'.

defeat-communism.rationale: Refused to be labelled anti-communist or communist and sought Soviet backing; rejected both blocs.

notes: Born 2 July 1925, killed 17 January 1961 (checked on Wikipedia). 'Congo, My Country' (1962) was found on archive.org (borrowing-only) but its text was not available, so it is not used. Economic positions are thin: his own words stress economic independence rather than a worked-out system, and he denied being a communist or socialist. Press and assembly restrictions in 1960 are recorded secondhand in Wikipedia.
